BiblicalUsage: Chamar is the Aramaic word for wine, and it shows up at two very different tables. Belshazzar drank wine before a thousand of his lords and praised gods of gold and silver from the temple vessels, on the very night his kingdom fell. In Ezra the same wine is listed among the supplies the king orders for the temple, given day by day without fail for the burnt offerings of the God of heaven.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe wine itself is neither holy nor cursed in these verses; what matters is the table it is poured at. At Belshazzar's feast it sealed a kingdom's judgment, and at the rebuilt temple it served worship. I hold that God gives good gifts to be used in His service, and the same gift turns to shame the moment it is lifted against Him.
